--- title: "Counting forwards (110)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_CONTAR_H_DELANTE_1O_DECENA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_CONTAR_H_DELANTE_1O_DECENA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Contar hacia delante (1.ª decena)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_CONTAR_H_DELANTE_1O_DECENA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Counting forwards (1–10), at age 5 (1,225 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .53 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2029 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | 6 (2029) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child starts counting from a given number. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 2029|Contar - Hacia Delante - 1ª Decena |Un estímulo por pantalla (discreto) | 6| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **2029.** Una serie de conteo (del 5 al 10); 2030–2032 tienen dos. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![2029 · Contar - Hacia Delante - 1ª Decena](../../figuras/plataforma/2029.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2029"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Counting the kittens on a picture card measures **counting of collections**: assigning a numeral to each object and knowing that the last one says how many there are (cardinality). Counting forwards within the first ten measures only the verbal sequence, without objects. Both are treated in more detail in the number knowledge framework. **What the evidence says:** - **Cardinality is one of the best early predictors.** In 197 children assessed at the start of preschool, knowledge of the cardinal value of numerals, fluency in the number sequence and digit recognition predicted mathematics at the end of the stage [@geary2016core]. In 128 British children, cardinality and receptive vocabulary explained the initial differences in mathematics [@cahoon2024cognitive]. - **In Spanish, the verbal sequence carries most weight.** In children followed from preschool to Grade 2, procedural counting was the task with the most weight in later mathematics achievement [@mercader2017basicas]. **What our data show.** Both tasks have a strong ceiling at age 5: 41–47% of children get all counting items right and 86% the whole sequence. That is why they discriminate poorly: AUC .43–.60 against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 and .45–.58 against low reading fluency. Consistency is moderate (α = .68 and .74) and the stability of counting is low (ρ = .19). Their reasonable use is to detect the few children who have not yet mastered counting in preschool. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.3| 2011| 159|2016/17 | 883| 0| 883| 34| | 5.3| 2012| 192|2017/18 | 342| 338| 0| 16| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 5.3| 338| 2012| 5.53| 1.37| 6| -3.02| 2.07| 86.09| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–6 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 5.3| 338|0–6 |0–6 |0–6 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .74. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Letter knowledge (5.3, r = .24). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .53. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .52–.54. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_CONTAR_H_DELANTE_1O_DECENA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .57 (1 time point; 325–325 children). Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([provisional criterion](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*), AUC .49. ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.3| 338| 2012| 1| 5| 6| 6| 6| 6| 6| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_CONTAR_H_DELANTE_1O_DECENA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 1,199| 0.022| 0.438| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 1,220| -0.004| 0.940| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 1,211| 0.112| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 1,225| 0.027| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Counting forwards (1–10)” (code 2029; LEEDUCA battery) assesses verbal number sequence. The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. It comprises 6 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .74 (N = 1,232, 6 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .52–.54. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
